classification.difficultyReason: Calculate missing class centres, choose suitable axes, and translate frequencies into touching bars and a polygon, retaining the zero-frequency class and closing endpoints.

content.prompt: Display the data using a frequency histogram and polygon using a class centre.

inlines.text: Draw touching bars centred at 9.5, 29.5, 49.5, 69.5 and 89.5, each of width 20, with heights 4, 2, 6, 3 and 5. Join the midpoints of their tops with straight lines. Extend the polygon to zero frequency at −10.5 and 109.5.

spec.description: Five touching histogram bars with an overlaid frequency polygon. Normalised horizontal coordinates 1–5 correspond to the supplied class centres, separated by 20. Outlined bars retain both constructions without decorative fill.
spec.mathematics: Class boundaries −0.5, 19.5, 39.5, 59.5, 79.5, 99.5; heights 4, 2, 6, 3, 5. Polygon closes at (−10.5,0) and (109.5,0).

answer.worked: The class centre is the midpoint of the class endpoints: $$\begin{align*}\text{Class centre}_1&=\frac{1+5}{2}=3\\\text{Class centre}_2&=\frac{6+10}{2}=8\\\text{Class centre}_3&=\frac{11+15}{2}=13\\\text{Class centre}_4&=\frac{16+20}{2}=18\\\text{Class centre}_5&=\frac{21+25}{2}=23\end{align*}$$ Draw touching bars of width 5 centred at these values, with heights $4,7,0,2,5$. Join $(3,4),(8,7),(13,0),(18,2),(23,5)$ with straight lines, extending to zero frequency at $-2$ and $28$. The class centred at 13 has no bar above the baseline.

spec.description: Five class intervals with touching histogram bars and an overlaid frequency polygon; the third interval has zero frequency. Normalised centres 1–5 correspond to 3, 8, 13, 18 and 23. Outlined bars omit decorative source fill and answer-label boxes.
